narrative: This round's fire and climate papers point to disturbance reshaping ecosystems: increasing fire severity is altering plant diversity assembly in dry conifer forests, while a 35-year record shows aboveground nitrogen pools rebuilding after stand-replacing fire. Climate work links greenhouse warming to more extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone, raising rainfall extremes in southern Africa. In movement and behaviour, step selection is being used to predict connectivity, and predation risk changes nut-caching behaviour and so tree establishment. Invasion studies show exotic dominance leaving microbial legacies that favour exotic plants, and horizon scanning flags future invaders for the Canary Islands. Conservation syntheses find that river barrier removal and stream restoration deliver gradual, uneven recovery, and sea-level rise threatens many terrestrial vertebrates. On methods, active learning for camera trap images and a machine-learning tool for detecting wildlife trade stand out.
